intent: Individually authored tasks preserve modifiers, conditions, completion and partial extent without inventing measurements.
picturePurpose: Original fictional partly-versus-wholly obstructed paths support extent comparison; exact ordering and progress labels remain in code, without real-route safety claims.

workshop.title: 排先后、看进度、辨部分
workshop.instruction: 先排句中先后，再比较接近完成与全部完成，最后分清部分和全部。

transfer.stem: Which notes preserve the condition, the unfinished work and the extent of the obstruction?
transfer.passage:
Getting the display ready
Our class was preparing a display for the school open day. I really enjoyed our quiet walk to collect ideas. After rain, one narrow path was very slippery. Fallen branches partly blocked it. Our teacher told us that the description did not establish whether the real route was safe to use.
Back at school, a box was quite light without the books. We did not weigh it. A rope was rather short for one task, but nobody gave its exact length. A metal handle became extremely hot; the note did not record a temperature.
We were told to let the paint dry completely before moving a frame. This was an instruction, not a report that the frame had already been moved. We had nearly finished preparing the display when the rain began again. Some work still remained.

The box had an exact stated weight; everything was already finished; branches blocked the whole path.
